title: Beginner Open-Chord Songs: Eleanor Rigby, Get Lucky, and Pearl Jam
summary: In this JustinGuitar video, the instructor curates beginner-friendly songs that align with the course’s open-chord focus, emphasizing C and Em while noting that G will be introduced in the next lesson. He highlights Eleanor Rigby as a first choice using C and Em, with a nod to interesting chord changes during barre sections and the flexibility to vary strumming patterns. He also covers Get Lucky by Daft Punk as a simplified, repetitive strummed progression based on Am–C–Em–D, pointing out D as a common hurdle. A brief mention of Pearl Jam illustrates how some favorites fit the course via chords already taught, specifically using C but not G. Viewers are encouraged to pick one song or rotate among several, and to check a website-listed set of recommended songs. Overall, the video emphasizes chord familiarity, careful changes, and practical strumming across recognizable tunes.
topics: practice strategy (one song vs rotating songs)

sections.title: Easy Songs for Beginners using the C Chord
sections.description: Justin introduces a set of beginner-friendly songs that align with lesson 5, noting that G will be introduced in the next lesson. He emphasizes practicing with chords learned (primarily C, with Em), and mentions a site list of recommended songs while inviting audience input for additional suggestions.

sections.title: Easy Songs for Beginners - Eleanor Rigby by The Beatles
sections.description: The first choice discussed is Eleanor Rigby, which uses C and Em. The instructor notes occasional chord changes in the middle of a barre and encourages learning those transitions, while suggesting that multiple strumming patterns can be applied. The Beatles are referenced as a cultural touchstone.
